is_private.desc: Whether the code channel is private. When omitted, the channel matches the privacy of `origin_channel_id`, or is public if no origin is given. An explicit value is always honored, even if it differs from the origin channel's privacy: passing `false` creates a public channel from a private origin.

name.desc: A friendly display name for the code channel. Optional when `origin_channel_id` and `origin_message_ts` are provided — in that case the channel is named from the origin message and re-titled automatically. Required when no origin link is given.

origin_channel_id.desc: The channel ID where the agent session was initiated from. Must be provided together with `origin_message_ts`. The channel must be accessible to the calling user and must not be externally shared (Slack Connect). When `team_id` is omitted with an org token, the channel is created in the same workspace as this origin channel. Pass `origin_channel_id` and `origin_message_ts` to link the session back to the triggering message. If either `origin_channel_id` or `origin_message_ts` cannot be resolved, the request fails with `invalid_origin_link` and no channel is created.

origin_message_ts.desc: The message timestamp in the origin channel that started the agent session. Must be provided together with `origin_channel_id`. The author of this message is automatically invited to the newly created code channel. Pass `origin_channel_id` and `origin_message_ts` to link the session back to the triggering message. If either `origin_channel_id` or `origin_message_ts` cannot be resolved, the request fails with `invalid_origin_link` and no channel is created.

session_id.desc: An opaque identifier for the agent session. When provided, the call is idempotent: if a channel already exists for this `session_id`, it is returned instead of creating a new one.

team_id.desc: Encoded team id to create the channel in. Required for org tokens when `origin_channel_id` is not provided. When omitted, the workspace is derived from the origin channel.

desc: Create a dedicated code channel for an agent session.

errors.channel_creation_failed: The code channel could not be created.
errors.channel_not_viewable: A channel exists for this session but the caller does not have permission to view it.
errors.feature_disabled: The caller is not authorized to create code channels. The app must be a recognized agent session app, or the user must have the feature enabled.
errors.invalid_agent: The agent bot user associated with the calling app is not a valid bot.
errors.invalid_origin_link: The origin link is invalid. Either origin\_channel\_id and origin\_message\_ts were not provided together, the channel does not exist or is not accessible to the caller, or the message was not found at the given timestamp.
errors.invite_failed: The channel was created but the agent bot could not be invited.
errors.name_or_origin_required: A name must be provided unless an origin link (origin\_channel\_id and origin\_message\_ts) is given to derive the channel name from.
errors.no_shared_workspace: No workspace could be found where both the app and the requesting user are present. The org app must have a workspace grant for at least one workspace the user belongs to.
errors.open_failed: The channel was created but could not be opened in the sidebar.
errors.origin_channel_externally_shared: The origin message is in an externally shared (Slack Connect) channel, DM, or group DM. Code channels cannot be created from a Slack Connect conversation.
errors.origin_channel_is_file_channel: The origin message is a comment on a file or canvas. Code channels cannot be created from a file channel — when the canvas belongs to a code channel, continue that session instead.
errors.restricted_action: The calling user is not permitted to create channels of the requested type in this workspace.
errors.user_not_enabled: The author of the origin message does not have the code channels feature enabled.
